correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening and upper Old Woman River
correspondence.finding: The detail original depicts the chosen opening in the upper valley directly labeled Old Woman River, with continuous channel linework running northeast and then north through the selected bends and entering side valleys. The regional overview connects this upper passage to the remaining northward river.
correspondence.name_scope: Old Woman River upper component; separate from the Unalakleet River name.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward middle Old Woman River valley
correspondence.finding: Repeated Old Woman River labels follow the continuous northward channel through the selected alternating bends and intervening tributary joins. The source distinguishes the longitudinal trunk from the side streams and depicts its through-connection across the middle valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Old Woman River and approach to Unalakleet
correspondence.finding: The mapped Old Woman River continues north along the lower confined valley and into the wider junction setting beside the Iditarod National Historic Trail. Its uninterrupted channel connects the middle valley with the named receiving river.
correspondence.name_scope: Old Woman River lower component, with no exact formal name-change vertex assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Old Woman–Unalakleet junction and westward turn
correspondence.finding: The map shows Old Woman River entering the larger Unalakleet River corridor. The selected route turns west with the receiving river, whose name is printed along the connected meandering channel. This is an observed channel junction rather than an inference from proximity or basin membership.
correspondence.name_scope: Junction between two separately named rivers; Unalakleet River is the downstream receiving-system identity.

correspondence.component_scope: West-southwest Unalakleet middle valley
correspondence.finding: The continuously depicted, repeatedly labeled Unalakleet River runs west-southwest through the selected valley. Tributary mouths, meander bends, side ponds and adjoining wetlands are visible; the through-river remains distinct from the nearby isolated waters and connects the upstream junction to the lower corridor.
correspondence.name_scope: Unalakleet River middle corridor; nearby ponds and tributaries are not aliases or additional candidate names.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Unalakleet and approach to the coastal lowland
correspondence.finding: The selected lower course corresponds to the continuous named Unalakleet River, which broadens and meanders west through the lowland. The overview and overlapping terminal detail show the intervening side-stream joins and the transition to the lower North River and South River junction setting. No selected through-lake, reservoir, glacier or engineered transfer is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower tributary junctions, Unalakleet estuary and actual coastal terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The terminal original shows North River and South River joining the named lower Unalakleet channel, its connected island-and-slough estuary south of the village, and the open coastal mouth. The selected final generalized segment crosses this same estuarine outlet setting to the Norton Sound shore. A unique current delta branch or exact shoreline crossing is not assigned. The BLM program account independently places the river terminal at Unalakleet on Norton Sound.
correspondence.name_scope: Mouth and estuary of the representative Unalakleet River system; coastal water and individual sloughs are not assigned the river scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern mountain opening and headward valley
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening follows an incised mountain valley and its westward bend toward the Nogolí impoundment setting. The imagery supplies continuous ordinary valley geography. Operator prose identifies El Molle and Chico as reservoir feeders, but does not establish which name belongs to this selected feeder; neither is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Approach through the Nogolí reservoir and dam setting
correspondence.finding: The incoming valley reaches the visible Nogolí reservoir and dam setting. IGN identifies Dique Nogolí and the water-footprint study places it on Río Nogolí. The reservoir is a separate component, with its western outlet leading toward the downstream river corridor. The independently documented aqueduct is distinguished from the selected downstream natural drainage.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward Río Nogolí corridor and southwest turn
correspondence.finding: The path below the impoundment follows the westward drainage labeled Río Nogolí on the original IGN sheet, then bends southwest at the western piedmont. The same corridor is visible in the imagery and belongs to the Nogolí drainage described by the provincial study.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward Cañada de Balde collector
correspondence.finding: The southward alluvial valley corresponds to the separately labeled Cda. de Balde on IGN. The imagery preserves the connected valley through its bends and joining-channel settings. This lower name is retained as its own component name; it is not silently replaced with Río Nogolí.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower collector and approach to the northern saline margin
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation follows the lower alluvial corridor to the northern Salina del Bebedero margin. IGN depicts the collector-to-pan receiving relationship and imagery shows the same broad entrance corridor and marginal saline terrain. Lateral channels are not separately selected or given the mainstem name; no external Chorrillos tributary is added.

correspondence.component_scope: Terminal saline-pan continuation and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The remaining selected display continuation and actual ending lie within the independently identified Salina del Bebedero. The pan entrance and receiving setting are observed, so absence of a mapped river line across its floor is not a material connector gap. The salina is a terminal waterbody/playa component, not a river-named reach, a surveyed river mouth or proof of permanent inundation.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening and wooded transfer to the northeastern lake inlet
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies among pasture and wooded drainage corridors northeast of the lake. Both overview and closer imagery expose multiple small corridors, but the westward through-link across the wooded section to the selected lake-entry branch cannot be established. Adjacent Río Blanco Las Cascadas and Río Blanco Arenal names are not transferred to this inlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastern lake entrance and Lago Llanquihue crossing
correspondence.finding: The selected continuation enters and traverses the same large lake toward its southwestern shore. Shoreline generalization and the conceptual line across open lake water are not interpreted as a narrow river channel or as new reach names. The link from the unconfirmed upper branch remains the preceding component’s gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern lake outlet and upper Maullín
correspondence.finding: Imagery shows the southwestern outlet continuing into the wooded and meandering river corridor through the settled and agricultural landscape. The conservation plan independently identifies Maullín as the lake outlet.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Maullín and approach to the second fragment
correspondence.finding: The selected westward bends and later southwestward reach remain in the same visible meandering valley toward the lower river. Wet and forested margins are recognized without asserting every bank or instantaneous flow path.

correspondence.component_scope: Mainstem fragment join
correspondence.finding: The end of the first fragment and beginning of the second occupy the same continuous lower river corridor; no tributary switch is inferred at the stored fragment boundary.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Maullín widening and actual selected terminal
correspondence.finding: The southward then westward selected continuation follows the broadening river and wetland/estuarine reach. The displayed endpoint remains within that broad estuarine corridor, upstream of the outer ocean mouth; the model’s sea class is not treated as proof that this point is the Pacific coastline. The source describes the farther regional continuation to the Pacific.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western opening and Rio Ouro Fino reach
correspondence.finding: The selected western opening follows a small feeder by Tesoura/Tezouras into the north–south channel through Itiúba and the Ouro Fino/Novo Horizonte setting. The older original labels this receiving channel Rio Ouro Fino; the newer Apuarema compilation confirms the ordinary connected drainage corridor. The small opening feeder itself has no established separate name.

correspondence.component_scope: Juru/Formosa turn from Ouro Fino toward Penedo
correspondence.finding: At the selected southern turn near Juru/Formosa, both originals draw Ouro Fino drainage separately from the river toward Penedo. The intervening east/northeast route follows or approaches an orange municipal boundary, not a continuously depicted watercourse. No acquired source establishes a natural, wetland, lake, reservoir or managed connector across this important selected through-link. This is a correspondence gap, not an assertion of a proved hydrologic impossibility or a request for exact bank/flow measurements.

correspondence.component_scope: Rio Penedo and receiving Rio das Almas
correspondence.finding: Beyond the gap, the northeast-running selected drainage corresponds to the mapped Penedo corridor and its meeting with Rio das Almas. Apuarema2020 directly labels Rio Penedo near Formosa and distinguishes Riacho Formoso arriving from the south. Riacho Formoso is bounded tributary context, not treated as an alias for the selected river or proof of the missing western connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Almas bends to Três Águas, Palmeiras and Wenceslau Guimarães
correspondence.finding: The source depicts the continuing Almas course through the Riachão do Canto/Rio da Lama tributary setting, around the southern bend near Formosa/Palmeiras and northeast past Três Águas into Wenceslau Guimarães. Adjacent labelled tributaries remain context only. The channel and joins are depicted without an intervening selected lake or reservoir passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern river to Nilo Peçanha
correspondence.finding: Overlapping originals follow the eastward river through Sapucaia/Barra de Paristo, Beira do Rio/Pedro Nunes, the southern bend near Paulista and northeast through Tachos/Cachoeira Grande to Nilo Peçanha. Nilo2020 directly prints Rio das Almas ou Jequié on this connected river. All selected intermediate bends and receiving tributary joins are included at ordinary corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal in the northward estuarine channel
correspondence.finding: From Nilo Peçanha the selected path turns north in the widened channel toward Taperoá and ends in that estuarine network south of the town. The source labels the connected coastal channel Rio Jequié and depicts widening/side-channel geography. The selected endpoint is not replaced by a farther open-Atlantic mouth. No present-day tidal direction, exact bank, gate operation or discharge claim is made.
